name: Jack Henry & Associates

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Sells core-banking, payments and digital software and processing to US community banks and credit unions; serves 7,200+ institutions, about 5,600 of them non-core clients; international under 1% of revenue.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: FY26 revenue $2,544M: cloud $816M, product delivery and services $295M, on-premise support $337M, processing $1,096M (43%). Segments: Core, Payments, Complementary, Corporate Services; Core is only $768M (+4.8%).

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Banks and credit unions; no client over 10% flagged and customers are diffuse; core clients up to $55B assets; average core bank client $1.42B assets.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: US almost entirely; revenue outside the US under 1%, so negligible currency exposure (a dollar rise does not hurt it); exposure is to US community-bank health.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Software, hosting and processing paid per account with 6-year core contracts and minimum payments; processing is 42.3% of Q1 FY27 revenue (+10.7%) and hosting +11.7%; clients pay monthly. Explained in two sentences.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Q1 FY27 GAAP operating margin 29.5% (28.5% a year ago); R&D 6.5% of revenue; FY26 capex plus capitalised software $251M (~10% of revenue); deferred revenue $333M (customers pay ahead); met or beat guidance in the last two quarters per CEO; margin guide 24.1-24.3% non-GAAP FY27 vs 23.9% FY26 (tough first-half comps).

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Inputs are mostly people (wage inflation named as a risk) plus cloud, licences and infrastructure; Q1 cost of revenue rose on personnel, cloud and AI costs. Private-cloud data centres run in multiple locations; image processing from two sites and statement printing from three centres, a modest chokepoint. Passes costs through multi-year per-account pricing, though repricing waits for renewals. Signal tags: wages (labour cost), rates (client budgets and settlement float income), tariffs/oil negligible.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Switching costs: a core conversion is a multi-year project; record 58 competitive core wins in FY26 including 14 banks above $1B assets; faster payments revenue +43.8% and digital +13.3% in Q1; cloud migration lifting hosting +11.7%.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Invisible to consumers; used daily by bank customers but under the bank's brand; reorder happens at contract renewal. Scored low because there is no consumer brand pricing power.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Named rivals: FIS, Fiserv, Corelation, Finastra. 58 competitive core wins in FY26 is a record; those rivals now show FIS pro forma growth 3.7% and Fiserv organic flat (industry file), versus Jack Henry non-GAAP +7.2%. Core segment non-GAAP growth only 4.9% in Q1; cores are a share-gain story but a slow one.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Guide FY27 non-GAAP revenue +6.6-7.4% with margin up. Payments segment +8.3% and complementary +8.4% non-GAAP in Q1. Bank count shrinking 3% a year (FDIC) caps new accounts; assets per client rising.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: FY26 operating cash flow $762M; free cash flow after capex and capitalised software about $507M (my calc); FY26 buybacks $448M at $152 avg; dividends $170M; ROIC 23.2% (company figure); debt $85M vs cash $25M. FY26 cash flow was helped by a $126M deferred-tax swing. Insider ownership and pay metrics not assessed in this pass.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Sticky mission-critical systems and gaining relevance as cloud and faster payments scale. Risks: bank consolidation, deconversions (revenue from clients leaving: $17.9M in Q1 vs $8.6M, a rising trend but billed as termination fees), AI-driven cost pressure, hiring costs.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 8-K Item 4.01 or 4.02 in the last 80 8-Ks; no NT filings or SEC comment letters since 2015; PwC clean opinion with one critical audit matter (revenue variable consideration); no material weakness. Non-GAAP only strips deconversion fees and an acquisition (about 3% of operating income).

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: wage costs rise, higher rates lift settlement float income but raise bank deposit costs. Slowdown: recurring contracts hold, defensive. Stagflation: defensive subscription core holds per industry file. Dollar: no exposure. Boom: bank tech budgets loosen but growth is already steady.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Regulated indirectly via bank examiners (clients' vendor oversight); no pending deal or docket found; cyber incident risk is the main regulatory tail. Nothing pending in filings checked.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: At $182.08 (up from $140-153 buyback prices), market cap $12.7B, EV about $12.7B, P/E about 26x FY26 EPS and 24x FY27 guide midpoint $7.49, FCF yield about 4.0%. Reverse DCF at 10% and 3% terminal: needs about 10% a year FCF growth for 10 years (11.5% if FCF is normalised to $460M), versus last-5-year FCF growth of about 10% a year (FY21 ~$311M to FY26 ~$507M) and a revenue guide of 7%. No cushion. Own 5-year multiple range and peer P/Es not computed in this pass.

status_reason: Quality B and a real share-gainer, but the price already assumes about 10% a year FCF growth for 10 years, matching its past, so there is no cushion and no clear mistake.

feedback.note: Jack Henry says bank tech spending is strong and its pipeline is robust (Q1 FY27), a defensive contradiction of the Slowdown fear; no sign of bank budget cuts yet. Client deconversion fees doubled to $17.9M in Q1 from $8.6M, consistent with bank M&A.
